newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC SQUANDER CHANCE OF GOING TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC SQUANDER CHANCE OF GOING TOP.

text.p: Celtic squandered the chance to take over from Rangers at the top of the Scottish premier division on Saturday when they were held to a 2-2 draw at home by Hearts.
Celtic also finished a disappointing afternoon with 10 men after Italian striker Paolo Di Canio was shown the red card seconds after scoring from a 77th minute penalty to put his side level at 2-2.
Di Canio was dismissed by the referee -- who also booked six other players -- after clashing with Steve Fulton. He was the 10th Celtic player to be sent off this season.
Rangers have the chance to stretch their lead to five points when they play at Aberdeen on Sunday.

In a match of high drama Hearts went ahead through a Colin Cameron header after 31 minutes. Brian O'Neil headed Celtic's first equaliser with a helping hand from Hearts' French goalkeeper Gilles Rousset two minutes before the break.
Neil McCann put Hearts 2-1 up after 64 minutes.
Rangers lead the standings with 29 points from 12 matches, followed by Celtic on 27 from 13, Aberdeen 22 from 13 and Hearts 20 from 14.

At the other end of the table bottom club Raith beat one-from-bottom Kilmarnock 1-0 thanks to a last-minute winner from Danny Lennon. Kilmarnock finished with 10 men after Jim McIntyre was sent off in the first half.
Darren Jackson scored twice -- once from the spot -- as Hibernian beat Motherwell 2-0 while Dundee United drew 1-1 with Dunfermline.
